claims.text: The initial RHEA is a disordered BCC solid solution without engineered nanoscale precipitates.
Advanced thermomechanical processing, such as rapid annealing or cyclic thermal treatment, can induce controlled precipitation in RHEAs.
The proposed processing will produce coherent nanoscale precipitates uniformly dispersed within the BCC matrix.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Obstructing dislocation motion hinders plastic deformation and strengthens the alloy.
Controlling precipitate size and distribution prevents the formation of unstable or brittle phases.
The controlled precipitate dispersion preserves thermal stability.
The controlled precipitate dispersion preserves irradiation stability.
The processed alloy will have higher yield strength than conventionally processed, precipitate-free RHEAs.
The processed alloy will have greater ductility than conventionally processed, precipitate-free RHEAs.
The processed alloy will retain phase stability during combined high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
Mechanical and stability improvements require a stable, coherent nanoprecipitate dispersion.
Significant precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency may eliminate the mechanical-performance benefits.
Significant precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency may eliminate the stability benefits.
The optimal precipitate size, volume fraction, and distribution for balancing strengthening with long-term thermal and irradiation stability are not yet precisely determined.
